newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bre-X seeks clarity on govt Busang stance - source. [CORRECTED 12:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bre-X seeks clarity on govt Busang stance - source. [CORRECTED 12:42 GMT]

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd (Corrects) is seeking clarification from Indonesia on what kind of a deal it has to do with Barrick Gold Corp to develop the Busang gold find, a source close to the negotiations said on Thursday.
A top Indonesian mining official said earlier Bre-X and Barrick had responded positively to a government letter recommending a 25-75 split in the Busang gold property.
"They are very positive," Umar Said, secretary-general of the mines department, told reporters after meetings with officials of both companies on Wednesday, the Indonesian deadline for an agreement.
But a source close to the negotiations said "responding positively does not mean an agreement".
"Bre-X wants to clarify with the Mines and Energy Ministry whether it is an instruction or just guidance," the source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, told Reuters.
"Bre-X has to answer to its shareholders...they will be upset if Bre-X has to give away 75 percent," the source said.
He said Bre-X was continuing to hold negotiations with Barrick, but declined to say if there had been any progress.
The source said, however, there was no quarrel over giving the Indonesian government a 10-percent stake in the find, estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.
The Mines and Energy Ministry suggested in a letter dated November 22 that Bre-X retain 25 percent while Barrick take a 75-percent stake to develop the property.
The Indonesian government has also sought a 10 percent stake in the property in East Kalimantan.
Asked about the government request, Umar said: "Yes, they want to give 10 percent to the Indonesian government."
"The next step is that they have to reach an agreement on a joint venture," he said.
Asked if they had made a positive response to the letter, the official replied: "Yes."
Umar said however the ministry had not yet received a formal reply from the companies.

The government had set a December 4 deadline for a response to the letter. Umar has said that if the two companies failed to reach a partnership agreement, the government would explore other ways to expedite development of the Busang find.

Bre-X has a partnership deal with PT Panutan Duta of the Panutan Group run by President Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto, under which Panutan would receive $40 million over 40 months plus a 10 percent stake in Busang's richest parts.

Barrick has teamed up with a construction company in the Citra Group of Suharto's eldest daughter, Siti Hardianti Rukmana, in what Barrick had said was a partnership "to prepare us for a potential mining development project".
The Mines Department's Umar said on Wednesday Barrick was selected to partner Bre-X to develop Busang because it was highly rated by the world mining community.
He also said applications for contracts of work by Bre-X for the richest parts of Busang were not among 68 others awaiting final approval from Suharto.
The source close to Bre-X said the government had agreed in principle to issue the contracts to Bre-X and that they had been endorsed by the Indonesian parliament along with the 68 others.
